title: How do we draw lines parallel to the segments a to h?
description: Eight segments are drawn on dot paper. The board copies each by counting its steps across and up or down, and finds that the segments with unusual steps are harder to draw by eye.
teaching_notes: One idea: to draw a parallel line, count the steps across and up of the given segment and repeat them from another dot. Lines that lean at the corner of a square are easy by eye.

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q4
video_script.why: The child knows parallel lines keep the same gap and now copies eight segments on dot paper.
video_script.substitution: Draw a parallel to each segment, the same way as the example in the book, by repeating its steps from another dot, and say which segments were hard.
video_script.anchor: Dot paper, thirteen dots by thirteen dots, with eight segments named a to h.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, some were hard, and the hard ones are e, f, g and h.

final_answer.value: (a) Yes. (b) The segments e, f, g and h. (c) Count the steps across and up and repeat them from another dot
final_answer.spoken: yes, some were hard, and the hard ones are e, f, g and h; count the steps across and up and repeat them from another dot

hold_back: (a) Yes. (b) The segments e, f, g and h. (c) Count the steps across and up and repeat them from another dot
maths_rules: a, b, c and d lean at the corner of a square: a is 1 across 1 down, b is 2 across 2 down, c is 3 across 3 up, d is 4 across 4 up, so they are easy to copy by eye
e is 1 across 3 down, f is 1 across 6 down, g is 5 across 2 up, h is 10 across 3 down; these have unusual steps and are harder by eye
to copy a segment, count its steps across and up or down, start at a new dot and take the same steps
the same steps keep the same gap, so the new segment is parallel
video_script.design: One dot paper stays on the stage. Each copied segment is drawn in a second colour beside the given one, with its steps written on it.
